title: Consume non-streaming Databricks SDK responses to release pooled HTTP connections
answers: Notebook hangs after many MLflow evaluations in a long-lived Databricks session
Why do MLflow requests through the Databricks SDK stop responding after repeated calls?
connection pool exhausted when calling api_client.do with raw=True in mlflow
leaked HTTP connections in mlflow rest_utils with use_databricks_sdk
body:
Symptom: In long-lived Databricks notebooks, MLflow calls (e.g. mlflow.genai.evaluate with LLM judges) silently hang after roughly 20 iterations; the connection pool runs dry.
Root cause: mlflow/utils/rest_utils.py:http_request (nested make_sdk_call) calls WorkspaceClient().api_client.do(..., raw=True), which streams the response, so the connection stays checked out of the pool until the body is read. Nothing read it for non-streaming callers.
Fix pattern: In make_sdk_call, after getting the response from raw_response["contents"]._response, read response.content when kwargs.get("stream", False) is false, then return the response. Streaming callers (stream=True) get the unconsumed response.
Constraints: Applies to every request routed through the Databricks SDK path (use_databricks_sdk=True). Do not drop the body read for non-streaming calls, and do not read the body for stream=True callers, because that would defeat streaming. Test coverage: tests/utils/test_rest_utils.py:test_databricks_sdk_response_is_consumed_unless_streaming.
applies: Any MLflow HTTP request sent via the Databricks SDK in mlflow/utils/rest_utils.py http_request; not for plain requests-session calls.
says: Databricks notebook evaluation jobs freeze without an error message after about twenty repeated runs.
Model evaluations with judge models silently stop responding during long-running notebook sessions.
The notebook gets stuck indefinitely when running multiple generative model assessments in sequence.
Prevent connection timeouts and stalls during extended automated model evaluation in notebooks.
Repeated evaluation calls in Databricks hang permanently instead of returning the benchmark scores.
search: MLflow HTTP requests sent via the Databricks SDK in mlflow/utils/rest_utils.py:http_request must read response.content on non-streaming calls to release pooled HTTP connections. Calling WorkspaceClient().api_client.do with raw=True streams responses, leaving connections checked out and exhausting the pool so long-lived Databricks notebooks silently hang during repeated calls like mlflow.genai.evaluate. In make_sdk_call, read response.content from raw_response['contents']._response when kwargs.get('stream', False) is false, but preserve unconsumed responses when stream=True. The fix applies strictly to SDK calls with use_databricks_sdk=True rather than plain requests-session calls, verified in tests/utils/test_rest_utils.py:test_databricks_sdk_response_is_consumed_unless_streaming.
